label: Explainer
description: Teaches one idea clearly, fact by fact.
structure: hook question → 3-5 facts or stats that build on each other → one clear takeaway
writing: curious and clear, second person, one idea per line, concrete numbers

editing.transitions: whip and slide, zoom on the big stat
editing.effects: highlight key words, shake only on the biggest number

label: Documentary
description: Calm narrator, context and history, room to breathe.
structure: cold open image → context → turning point → consequences → reflective close
writing: measured, warm narrator voice, past tense for history, quotes from real people

editing.effects: slow push-in, vignette on emotional beats

label: Story
description: A narrative with a character, a problem and a turn.
structure: meet the character → what they want → the obstacle → the turn → resolution or twist
writing: present tense storytelling, a named character, sensory details, dialogue-like lines; facts serve the story

editing.cuts: follow the story beats, faster at the obstacle, a held beat before the twist
editing.transitions: cuts within a scene, flash or whip between scenes
editing.effects: typewriter for inner thoughts, punch-in on the turn

label: Top-N list
description: Countdown of ranked items, one per segment.
structure: hook promising the list → items counting down (#5 … #1), each with a stat or fact → #1 payoff
writing: punchy, numbered headlines ('#3 · …'), one surprising detail per item

label: Quick clip
description: 15-25 s viral-style short with one punchline.
structure: scroll-stopping hook in the first second → 2-4 rapid beats → punchline or loop back to the hook
writing: very short lines (≤ 10 words), internet-native tone, one joke or surprise

label: How-to
structure: what you'll make or learn → Step 1 … Step N (one action each) → result and one pro tip
writing: imperative and friendly ('Grate the ube.'), exact quantities and times, no fluff

editing.cuts: one step per segment, hold long enough to read

label: Showcase
description: Hero shots of a product, place or creation; few words, big visuals.
structure: dramatic reveal → 3-4 features as benefits → hero shot with name and call to action
writing: minimal, confident, short benefit lines, no lists of specs

editing.cuts: cinematic holds on the reveal, quicker on features

label: News recap
description: What happened, why it matters, what's next.
structure: headline → what happened (who, what, when) → key numbers → reactions → what's next
writing: neutral and precise, attributed claims ('according to …'), no speculation

label: Comedy skit
description: Lighthearted take with jokes, still accurate.
structure: relatable setup → escalating jokes, each carrying a real fact → callback punchline
writing: playful, self-aware, Taglish welcome for PH topics, punchlines at the end of lines

editing.cuts: comic timing: a beat of silence before punchlines

label: Cinematic Flavor-Wash Product Spot
description: Short music-only product teaser that moves continuously through bold flavor-coded color worlds around a single drink can, then resolves on a clean white brand card.
structure: Hook on the product in a lush color field → cycle of flavor-themed color scenes (green, orange, pink, lilac, repeat) → white end card with logo/CTA.
writing: No voiceover. Minimal on-screen text: flavor names or one-word descriptors, then brand name and short tagline on the end card.

editing.cuts: Fast hard cuts about every 0.8 s (~72 per minute), often hidden inside colour washes or whip-pan hand-offs between flavour sets.
editing.transitions: Seamless color washes, whip-pan or match-move hand-offs between flavor sets, final fade/flash to white.
editing.captions: None for speech; sparse, clean sans-serif labels kept small and centered or lower-third.
editing.effects: Slow orbit and push-in on the can, macro detail, floating fruit/ingredients, splashes, soft shallow depth of field, glossy highlights.

source.title: CINEMATIC PRODUCT VIDEO | Go Good Drinks

label: Late-Night Cinematic Mood Piece
description: Quiet, atmospheric short film: one unbroken, slow-moving take of a solitary late-night ritual, low-key lighting, muted teal-green shadows, minimal words.
structure: Fade up from black → slow build of one quiet moment → gentle peak in brightness mid-piece → dims back → fade to black.
writing: Near-silent. One short, intimate dedication-style line addressed to night owls; no narration or dialogue beyond that.

editing.cuts: None; one continuous shot with slow camera drift instead of edits.
editing.transitions: Fade from black at open, fade to black at close; light changes carry the rhythm.
editing.captions: Minimal, small centered serif or thin sans text, appears once, lowercase, soft fade in/out.
editing.effects: Crushed blacks, cool teal-green grade, shallow depth of field, soft film grain, gentle vignette, steam/practical-light highlights.

source.title: 2 AM COFFEE - A short film | Sony FX3 | 4K

label: Whiteboard Doodle Mechanism Explainer
description: A one-minute hand-drawn explainer that follows one drug through the body as a single continuous story. A gut-level hook leads into the cell-entry and exit steps, then a feedback "villain" that locks the door, then a dosing-schedule fix, and it ends on a quick recap flow.
structure: Cold-open hook with a personified quip → step-by-step mechanism (entry, transit, exit, carrier to destination) → problem twist (hormone feedback blocks pathway, payload lost) → practical fix with one hard stat → recap summary flow chaining every step.
writing: Short, declarative narration in the present tense. Molecules and cells are cast as characters (doors, locks, factories, gatekeepers) with brief spoken asides. Each sentence covers one step. Technical names are kept but explained by their role. There is a single quantified takeaway, and the closing recap is written as an arrow chain.

editing.cuts: No hard cuts. The video is one continuous canvas, with new elements drawn in or the view panning and zooming to the next region.
editing.transitions: The camera pans or zooms across one whiteboard. Elements are drawn on with a hand stroke or wiped and redrawn, and the background clears to white for the recap.
editing.captions: Hand-lettered labels sit on the key structures (channel, door, hormone, carrier). Bold callouts appear for the stat and the summary arrows. There are no full burned-in subtitles.
editing.effects: Line-draw reveals, light character bobbing, and a lock or padlock icon snapping shut. Particles move along paths with arrows. One cell sloughs off with a small wobble, and the payload is shown flowing into a factory.

source.title: Ferrous Sulfate — How It Works (Animated Doodle Explainer)
